answer: One concrete defense is staking: each agent must post a bond of scarce collateral—think felled timber locked on-ledger—before it can trade. Spinning up a grove of fake identities then means funding each clone separately, so cost scales linearly with the Sybil count. An attacker chasing a summit of a thousand accounts must lock a thousand bonds; any clone caught cheating is slashed and loses its stake, so honest agents beat cheap fakes on pure economics.
